subject: ent
title: Rhinitis and nasal polyps

steps.tx: **Rhinitis** is nasal mucosal inflammation causing blockage, discharge, sneezing and itch. Allergic rhinitis divides seasonal (pollens) from perennial (house dust mite, animal dander) with IgE mediated mast cell degranulation producing immediate sneeze and late congestion; pale boggy turbinates and allergic crease support it. Non allergic, occupational, hormonal and drug induced (rhinitis medicamentosa from decongestant overuse) forms mimic it.
steps.say: Itchy sneezy watery nose with triggers means allergic rhinitis. Decongestant spray addiction causes its own rhinitis.

steps.tx: First line allergic therapy is allergen avoidance plus daily **intranasal corticosteroid** (correct aim outward technique), with non sedating antihistamines for sneeze and itch and saline irrigation as adjunct. Immunotherapy (subcutaneous or sublingual) modifies disease in severe selected cases with proven dominant allergen. Antibiotics treat no rhinitis without bacterial sinusitis evidence.
steps.say: Daily nasal steroid aimed outward is the backbone. Antihistamines help sneeze; immunotherapy reshapes severe allergy.

steps.tx: **Chronic rhinosinusitis** persists beyond twelve weeks with blockage, discharge, facial pain and smell loss, divided by polyp presence. Nasal polyps are pale grape like oedematous prolapses from ethmoid mucosa (middle meatus), bilateral usually, painless and insensate unlike red tender turbinates. Samter triad links polyps, asthma and aspirin sensitivity; cystic fibrosis and allergic fungal disease underlie selected cases.
steps.say: Pale painless grapes in both noses are polyps, not turbinates. Polyps plus asthma plus aspirin sensitivity is Samter triad.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Polyp and sinusitis care escalates from saline and intranasal steroids (drops or high volume delivery to sinuses) through short oral steroid bursts in severe polyp disease, to endoscopic sinus surgery opening drainage pathways when medical therapy fails, with biologics (anti IgE, IL4 or IL5 pathways) for recurrent severe polyps with asthma in specialist programmes. CT sinuses (Lund Mackay) plans surgery; it does not diagnose rhinitis.
steps.say: Steroids shrink polyps; surgery opens sinuses when sprays fail; biologics serve recurrent polyp asthma patients.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Red flags rewrite the pathway: unilateral polyp or mass (antrochoanal polyp from maxillary sinus in youth, inverted papilloma or malignancy in older adults) needs imaging and biopsy pathway, orbital pain or swelling and neurological signs mean complicated sinusitis, and epistaxis dominant disease suggests vascular or neoplastic causes. Anosmia after viral infection (including post COVID) is usually mucosal or olfactory neuronal and often recovers with smell training.
steps.say: One sided polyp is not routine: image it. Eye swelling with sinusitis is an emergency, not rhinitis care.
